look_here_first: Start with a mature capsule: the leathery surface is usually short-prickly or warty. On a flower, check whether stamens project conspicuously beyond petals (about twice petal length). Opposite palmately compound leaves establish buckeye, but do not separate Aesculus species.

taxonomic_note: POWO accepts Aesculus glabra Willd. and recognizes var. glabra and var. arguta; source is species-level. No unverified variety assignment. Aesculus × bushii is an accepted A. glabra × A. pavia hybrid and may be intermediate.

morphology_keys.habit: Deciduous small to medium tree with stout twigs and large terminal buds.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, palmately compound, usually 5–7 serrate leaflets; leaves alone overlap A. pavia.
morphology_keys.flowers: Terminal erect panicles; stamens markedly exserted, approximately twice petal length. Petals often pale green-yellow, but color is secondary.
morphology_keys.fruits: Leathery round capsules usually short-spiny or warty (occasionally nearly smooth), with glossy brown seeds and pale hilum.

comparisons.key_distinctions: A. pavia typically has smooth capsules and stamens about petal length or barely exserted; A. × bushii may be intermediate and requires caution. Cultivated horse-chestnut has different flower and bud traits. Ungnadia (Mexican buckeye) has pinnate, not palmately compound, leaves and a three-valved capsule. Flower color alone is unreliable.
